description: 2nd connection. 1st connection (2026-09-28T15:39:57Z) was CONFIRMED SUCCESS on every structural question it set out to test: TESTKIT (embedded SQL in a NOMAIN module, SET OPTION placed after the module-level D-specs) compiled and ran; CHGCURLIB1 put TESTRES in &LIB (not <USER>1); the case-00 deliberate failure sent its QMHSNDPM(*ESCAPE) message and the wrapper's own RUNTSTJUCSRV step never logged a FAILED marker afterward (strong evidence MONITOR caught it and TSTJUCSRV's mainline ran to completion rather than aborting); TSTZAISRV's 11 assertions ALL PASSED, including direct confirmation that OVRDBF+OVRSCOPE(*JOB) really redirected ZAISRV's internal ZAIKOM open to the QTEMP copy (TESTRES showed the seeded 7, not the real 45) (the discriminating evidence for the override working is TESTRES itself, not the real table's own final value: TSTZAISRV's own 5 cases are deliberately net-zero, so the real &LIB/ZAIKOM would have ended back at 45 either way, whether or not the override actually redirected anything - the shared-zaikom-check collect below is a supporting check that the real table is at its expected value, not independent proof the override worked). No TXRESET needed. ONE real bug found and fixed (src/qrpglesrc/testkit.sqlrpgle, this connection includes the fix): testInit() used to DELETE FROM TESTRES every call, on the assumption one test-case program calls it once per connection - TSTZAISRV's own testInit() call silently wiped TSTJUCSRV's just-logged 11 rows (00 through 10B) before the collect step could read them, so the 1st connection's TESTRES collect only ever showed TSTZAISRV's rows. testInit() is now create-only (never deletes); this manifest adds its own explicit CLEARTESTRES step (same pattern the CL wrapper already uses for VFYLOG) so THIS connection starts from a clean table and both programs' rows survive together in the final collect. Everything else below is unchanged from the 1st connection (all three objects already compiled with Highest Severity 00; REPLACE(*YES) makes recompiling them here harmless) - this connection's only real purpose is observing TSTJUCSRV's own 13 rows (cases 00-10B) for the first time, now that they will not be overwritten. POST-CONNECTION HOUSEKEEPING (2026-09-28, after both connections above): case 00 (the deliberate failure) moved from solutions/08-04/tstjucsrv.rpgle into src/tstjucsrv-faildemo.rpgle in this same verify directory (Q0613V pattern, verify/part06-1314-sql/src/q0613v.sqlrpgle) so the shipped solution stays a clean, all-passing artifact - this manifest now transfers that verify-only variant AS TSTJUCSRV, unchanged in every other respect from what the 1st/2nd connections above actually ran.

steps.label: CPTESTKITM
steps.cmd: CRTSQLRPGI OBJ(&LIB/TESTKIT) SRCFILE(&LIB/QRPGLESRC) SRCMBR(TESTKIT) OBJTYPE(*MODULE) COMMIT(*NONE)

steps.label: CPTESTKITS
steps.cmd: CRTSRVPGM SRVPGM(&LIB/TESTKIT) MODULE(&LIB/TESTKIT) EXPORT(*SRCFILE) SRCFILE(&LIB/QSRVSRC) SRCMBR(TESTKIT) ACTGRP(*CALLER) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.label: CPTESTKITBD
steps.cmd:
CHKOBJ OBJ(&LIB/TESTKITBD) OBJTYPE(*BNDDIR)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF9801) EXEC(CRTBNDDIR BNDDIR(&LIB/TESTKITBD))
ADDBNDDIRE BNDDIR(&LIB/TESTKITBD) OBJ((*LIBL/TESTKIT *SRVPGM))

steps.label: CPTSTJUCSRV
steps.cmd: CRTBNDRPG PGM(&LIB/TSTJUCSRV) SRCFILE(&LIB/QRPGLESRC) SRCMBR(TSTJUCSRV) DFTACTGRP(*NO) ACTGRP(*NEW) BNDDIR((*LIBL/JUCSRVBD) (*LIBL/TESTKITBD)) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.label: CPTSTZAISRV
steps.cmd: CRTBNDRPG PGM(&LIB/TSTZAISRV) SRCFILE(&LIB/QRPGLESRC) SRCMBR(TSTZAISRV) DFTACTGRP(*NO) ACTGRP(*NEW) BNDDIR((*LIBL/ZAISRVBD) (*LIBL/TESTKITBD)) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.label: QTEMPZAIKOM
steps.cmd: CRTDUPOBJ OBJ(ZAIKOM) FROMLIB(&LIB) OBJTYPE(*FILE) TOLIB(QTEMP) DATA(*YES)

steps.label: SEEDQTEMP
steps.cmd: RUNSQL SQL('UPDATE QTEMP/ZAIKOM SET ZASU = 7 WHERE ZASHO = ''P00001''') COMMIT(*NONE)

steps.sql: SELECT SEQ, TESTNM, EXPECTED, ACTUAL, RESULT FROM &LIB/TESTRES ORDER BY SEQ
SELECT COUNT(*) AS TOTAL_CNT, SUM(CASE WHEN RESULT = 'PASS' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS PASS_CNT FROM &LIB/TESTRES
SELECT ZASHO, ZASU FROM &LIB/ZAIKOM WHERE ZASHO = 'P00001'
